turns.assessment: The decisive signature is the simultaneous approximately 77–78 ps DGD increase on many independent channels, followed immediately by OTU_LOF and widespread service loss. The affected channels converge on the S04→S14 OMS, while amplifier powers and pump currents did not change, strongly favoring DGD_RISE in one of its six fibre spans over an amplifier or power-loss fault. There is no intermediate DGD measurement to distinguish which span is responsible, so no individual repair location reaches the 80% commitment threshold.

proposals.rationale: Span 1 of the S04→S14 OMS is common to the affected direction and could produce the common large DGD step without changing amplifier telemetry.
Span 2 is equally consistent with the receiver-side DGD increases; there is no span-level DGD telemetry to separate it from the other spans.
Span 3 lies on the common S04→S14 optical path and a DGD rise here would affect all traversing channels while leaving amplifier powers stable.
Span 4 is a viable source of the approximately 78 ps common DGD increase, but cannot be uniquely localized from endpoint observations.
Span 5 is common to the failed channels in the S04→S14 direction and is observationally indistinguishable from the other spans.
Span 6 immediately precedes S14 and could account for the DGD jump seen at S14 receivers, but no evidence specifically favors it over spans 1–5.

score.why: truth not in the reported set
